title: Rast wins Hungaroring Race 2 from pole and takes the points lead
dek: René Rast converted pole into victory for Audi, passing Mattias Ekström late in the race, while Maxime Martin climbed from the back to third and Lucas Auer left Hungary pointless.

chapters.title: A Saturday to forget for Audi
text: Saturday had gone to plan for everybody except Audi. Paul di Resta won Race 1 from 13th for Mercedes-AMG after an early stop and a well-timed safety car, with BMW’s Timo Glock and Bruno Spengler beside him on the podium, while Audi’s first five places on the grid were turned into fourth and fifth at best. Jamie Green’s seventh place was taken away after a Mercedes protest over a sealed gap in the front diffuser of his car.

Lucas Auer still led the championship on 69 points, but the weights shifted for Sunday: after their race pace on Saturday, the Audis had to run 10 kg heavier than the BMWs and Mercedes. Audi were left to prove that they could win with it.

chapters.title: Rast doubles up on pole, with Wittmann alongside
text: René Rast took pole for the second time in two days, with 1:34.740, despite the Audis carrying the extra ballast. It was the narrowest of margins at the top: the reigning champion Marco Wittmann had sat provisionally on pole in the closing minutes and finished second at 1:34.803, 0.063 seconds off, putting a BMW on the front row for the first time in the weekend and more than four tenths clear of his nearest team-mate, Glock.

Behind Wittmann came four Audis: Ekström third on 1:34.896, Nico Müller fourth, Mike Rockenfeller fifth and Green sixth. Auer was seventh and best of the Mercedes, directly behind Green, his closest rival for the title. Glock, Augusto Farfus and Tom Blomqvist completed the top ten. Gary Paffett qualified 11th and Saturday’s winner di Resta 12th, followed by Robert Wickens and Edoardo Mortara. Duval, Engel and Spengler filled the next places, and Maxime Martin, who had retired on Saturday, started last of the 18.

chapters.title: Early stops split the field
text: Rast made a clean start and led into the first corner. Wittmann got away slowly from second and lost the place to Müller. After a Saturday in which stopping early had paid off, a good part of the field decided to do the same. Martin, starting last, came in at the end of the first lap for his mandatory tyre change, and Rockenfeller and Ekström followed within the first four laps.

Auer pitted on lap 7, but the stop went wrong: he left the car badly positioned in his box and the mechanics were slow to finish the right-rear wheel. Di Resta and Glock stopped a lap later, and Green on lap 9, rejoining just behind di Resta. Maro Engel, who stayed out when the others stopped, led for a time with the fastest laps on the track, though he had been given a five-second penalty that he would have to serve at his own stop.

chapters.title: Ekström’s early stop puts him ahead
text: Rast, Müller and Wittmann, the leading trio, stayed out until around laps 10 to 12, more than five laps after Ekström. That decided the order: when Rast came out of the pits Ekström was ahead of him, and once the stops had played out the Audi from Abt led with Rast behind and Martin, on his early tyres, third from the back of the grid. Müller and Wittmann followed.

Engel took his stop and penalty on lap 19 and dropped to the back of the field. With a quarter of an hour to go the order was Ekström, Rast, Martin, Müller, Wittmann and di Resta, with the gaps barely changing on a circuit where passing is so hard. Green then picked off di Resta and Wittmann with two clean moves to take fifth place, leaving di Resta to slip back to sixth.

chapters.title: Rast passes Ekström at the first corner
text: With four laps to go Rast made his move, pulling alongside Ekström into the first corner and taking the lead, five minutes before the flag. Ekström had no answer and finished 1.041 seconds behind after 35 laps, having had, as he put it, little left to defend with. Rast had a first DTM victory, in 58:01.592, and with it the lead of the championship.

Martin, who had started 18th, held off Müller for third by 0.355 seconds, which spared Audi a podium sweep. Müller was fourth, Green fifth and di Resta sixth as the best Mercedes, with Glock, Wickens, Paffett and Rockenfeller completing the top ten; five of the ten were Audis. Ekström set the fastest lap, 1:36.725 on lap 5. Wittmann, who had been running sixth, lost two laps near the end and was classified 17th, and Auer, the only retirement, was out after 23 laps.

chapters.title: The leadership changes hands by a single point
text: Rast’s first words on the radio were simply “Mega! This is incredible, I can’t believe it.” Afterwards he said he had worked towards a win like this for ever, that Ekström had been fair in defending his position, and that it was too early to think about the title. The points lead, he added, was something special that he would not have dared dream of before the season. Rast moved to 70 points, with Auer a single point behind after six of the season’s 18 races and Green third in the table.

Ekström accepted second place in a sporting manner. His early stop, he said, had given him a huge chance of winning, but he had little left to fight with at the end and Rast simply waited for his moment. He called Rast the faster man and said he deserved the win. For Audi, five cars in the top ten were a large step back up after a Saturday that had begun with a front-row lock-out and ended with Green’s exclusion, and Green himself recovered to fifth with two decisive passes.

Martin was the other big winner. He had retired from Saturday’s race after the contact with Blomqvist, and by stopping on the opening lap he went from the back of the grid to a podium, which he called a good response to the day before; he said he had been flat-out from the start but had not expected to end up there. It was the second BMW podium of the weekend after Glock and Spengler on Saturday. For Mercedes it was a hard day: Auer, who had arrived as the championship leader, scored nothing in Hungary after a botched stop and an early exit on Sunday, and di Resta’s sixth place was the best the brand could manage a day after his win.

Wittmann’s weekend ended on a sour note, too, as he lost his sixth place when the car failed late on. Engel’s race was undone by a five-second penalty he served at his stop. The championship now heads to the Norisring for the fourth round of nine, with races on 1–2 July, and Rast, in his first full DTM season, goes there as leader by one point from Auer.

facts.v: René Rast won from pole in 58:01.592 over 35 laps, 1.041 seconds ahead of Mattias Ekström, for the first victory of his DTM career.
